analysis.one_liner: Adani Power is India's largest private thermal power generator, running coal-based plants across several states and recently adding capacity through the Jaiprakash Associates insolvency acquisition.
analysis.whats_happening: Adani Power's board meets on 23 October 2026 to approve Q2/H1 FY27 results, with an analyst call on 26 October - both inside the next two weeks. The last reported quarter (Q1 FY27, April-June 2026) was the company's strongest ever: PAT of ₹4,867 crore (+47% YoY) and EBITDA of ₹8,369 crore (+36% YoY), helped by the completed acquisition of Jaiprakash Associates' power assets (a 24% stake in Jaiprakash Power Ventures plus the 180 MW Churk plant, for over ₹4,193 crore combined). Separately, SEBI closed a Hindenburg-linked disclosure case in September 2026 against five other Adani group listed firms (not Adani Power itself) for a token ₹1.5 crore, without admission of guilt.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a coal power company that sells electricity to state utilities and on exchanges, and it has been growing fast - both the plants are running harder (plant load factor jumped to 78% from 67% a year ago) and profits have surged. The tension: none of this profit has ever reached shareholders as a dividend, and the company is taking on meaningfully more debt to fund acquisitions like the Jaiprakash assets. So you're trusting management to keep reinvesting well rather than being paid out directly.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026): revenue ₹17,936 crore (+26.6% YoY), EBITDA ₹8,369 crore (+36% YoY), PAT ₹4,867 crore (+47% YoY), on 16.9% higher power sold (28.8 BU) and a PLF jump to 78% from 67%. Q4 FY26 (Jan-Mar 2026) is less clean: some reports show headline revenue up ~10% to ₹15,989 crore, but revenue from operations was effectively flat (₹14,223 crore vs ₹14,237 crore a year earlier) - these are not strictly comparable framings. Below that noise, EBITDA still grew a healthy 27% YoY to ₹6,498 crore and PAT rose sharply (64% YoY per some sources) to ₹4,271 crore, so Q4 looks margin-led rather than volume-led, while Q1 FY27 was both volume- and margin-led. FY26 full-year PAT was ₹12,971 crore.
analysis.performance_read: Returns have been exceptional: +198% over 3 years and +698% over 5 years, versus Nifty's +16.6%/+24.5% and peer NTPC's +40%/+148% over the same periods - even the 1-year return of +25% beats a falling Nifty (-9.2%). The stock did a 1:5 split in September 2025 (face value ₹10 to ₹2), which is already reflected in these per-share return figures, not a demerger or spin-off, so no return-understatement adjustment is needed. The stock is down 21.1% from its 27 May 2026 peak of ₹248.91 to the current ₹196.50 - this is a price correction after a very large run-up, not evidence of a crash or a corporate-action distortion.
analysis.valuation_read: Sources disagree on the exact P/E, ranging from about 26.6x to 31.6x - treat that band as the honest number rather than picking one. That is a premium valuation for a thermal generator, and the reason is growth: PAT has been rising sharply quarter on quarter and the company is expanding capacity via acquisitions. Whether that premium is justified depends on whether the growth holds - ROE (22.8%) and ROCE (19.5%) are currently below their own 3-year averages (45% and 25.7% respectively), suggesting returns on capital have moderated even as the growth narrative strengthens elsewhere.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is now a mix of volume and margin, not margin alone. Q1 FY27 saw power sold up 16.9% YoY with the fleet running much harder (PLF 78% vs 67%), a genuine volume gain tied to strong all-India demand growth (+8.8% YoY) from heatwaves. Q4 FY26, by contrast, had almost flat core revenue from operations but a 27% EBITDA jump - that quarter's growth was margin-led. The Jaiprakash acquisition adds further capacity (2,220 MW of thermal/hydro plus the 180 MW Churk plant) but is inorganic, not same-asset growth.
analysis.health_read: Net debt rose from ₹31,023 crore (March 2025) to ₹45,022 crore (March 2026) - a 45% jump, largely funding the Jaiprakash acquisition and capacity additions. Debt-to-equity sits at a moderate ~0.91x and interest cover is a comfortable ~5.1x, and EBITDA has been growing faster than revenue, which is a healthy sign. Whether operating profit is converting cleanly into free cash flow after this debt-funded expansion is Not verified - check on Screener. The bigger watch item here is financial risk from the pace of debt-funded acquisitions, not core business/operating risk, which looks solid given rising PLF and demand.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters hold 74.96% (47.2% Indian, 27.76% foreign), unchanged as of March 2026, with a stable and low pledge of 1.81% of promoter shares. FIIs hold 11.73% and retail holds 9.62%, but domestic institutions (DIIs - mutual funds, insurers) hold just 0.05%, which is unusually low for a company of this size - there is effectively no meaningful domestic institutional (mutual fund/LIC-type) presence on the register, worth noting plainly rather than glossing over.
strengths: Q1 FY27 PAT of ₹4,867 crore, up 47% YoY, the company's strongest quarter on record
Plant load factor jumped to 78% from 67% YoY, showing much better asset utilisation
Stock has beaten both the Nifty and peer NTPC by a wide margin over 1, 3 and 5 years
Promoter holding stable at 74.96% with a low, unchanged pledge of 1.81%
watchpoints: Net debt up 45% YoY to ₹45,022 crore (Mar-26) from ₹31,023 crore (Mar-25), funding the Jaiprakash acquisition
No dividend has ever been paid despite years of now-large profits
Stock is down 21.1% from its May 2026 peak and has underperformed the Nifty and peer over the last 3 months (-9.3% vs -4.5%/-7.1%)
Domestic institutional ownership is just 0.05% - almost no mutual fund or insurer conviction despite the large market cap
analysis.one_thing: The 23-26 October 2026 Q2/H1 FY27 results and management's commentary on how the Jaiprakash-driven rise in net debt will be managed alongside continued PLF gains.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 and FY26 full-year PAT/EBITDA figures cross-checked across multiple outlets (Business Standard, IIFL, PSU Connect, Equitybulls) and agree closely. Q4 FY26 headline revenue growth (10%) conflicts with the revenue-from-operations figure (flat YoY) - both are reported here with the discrepancy flagged rather than resolved. P/E estimates range 26.6x-31.6x across sources; no single figure was treated as definitive. Net debt, ROE/ROCE and debt-to-equity are from third-party aggregators (Tijori, Gurufocus) and not cross-verified against the company's own filing - treat as indicative. Dividend figures (null/none) match the verified market data provided.
